items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: John Hammond was very kind to me and he gave me quite a lot of music of Bessie’s.

ctx.x: Was there a language, not a barrier but some of the things that Bessie Smith may have sung, even if you understood what she was saying, that there was a new phrase in there that maybe wasn’t common to English.

Yeah, we were not hip to a lot of these things, and certainly even today. John Hammond was very kind to me and he gave me quite a lot of music of Bessie’s. And I was pleased to see in some of the written words, the words that I’d been singing, lyrics I’d been singing, that everybody sort of who’d been singing. You know a lot of the singers who sing the Bessie Smith material had been singing incorrect words. Just sort of you made them up as an educated guess. But there are certainly words that were indigenous not…
I think it’s so great that Bessie Smith lands in the north of England and falls on someone’s ears like that. I just love that story.
